answer: I'd like to talk about a fairly modest purchase that has turned out to be surprisingly useful. Something I bought recently that I am delighted with is a good-quality water bottle designed to keep drinks cold for hours. It's an insulated steel bottle in dark green, just the right size to fit in the side pocket of my bag. I bought it from an online shop after comparing a few options, and it arrived at our flat within a couple of days. I bought it because I had been trying to drink more water and stay healthier. I used to go through half the working day without drinking anything, and I'd often come home in the evening feeling tired and dehydrated, especially in summer. It sounds trivial, but it has genuinely improved my daily routine. What makes me so happy with it is how well it actually works; my water stays refreshingly cold even in the intense heat. During the hottest months, when the afternoons are almost [[unbearable]], that makes a real difference. It has proved far more [[practical]] than I expected. The build quality is excellent, so it feels [[durable]] and worth the money. Beyond the practical benefit, it has genuinely encouraged me to develop a healthier habit, which is an unexpected bonus. Honestly, it is one of those small, [[sensible]] purchases that quietly makes life a little better. I now carry it everywhere I go. I think the most [[satisfying]] purchases are often the modest, useful ones rather than the flashy, expensive ones. It has quickly become an essential part of my daily kit.

followUps.q: Do you usually think carefully before buying things?
followUps.answer: Yes, usually. I compare a few options, read reviews and ask myself whether I'll actually use it. That habit has saved me from quite a few [[impulsive]] purchases over the years.

followUps.q: Do you prefer shopping online or in person?
followUps.answer: It depends. For practical items like this bottle, online is quicker and often cheaper, but for clothes or anything I want to touch and try, I still prefer going to a shop.

note: Added description, where he bought it (online) and the reason (hot summers, not drinking enough); new mark 'unbearable'.
